boards.title: Action summary · know what it is about before you act
boards.heading: Every found action says what it is about, and a click shows the rest
boards.intro: “I have no idea about what it is about, where’s coming from until I add it to the todo, create a slack msg, or create a draft jira.” Every action found in a note or an Ask answer now carries a summary of two to four plain sentences: what it is about, the context needed to act, who is involved, and what was asked or decided and by when. It is written when the action is found, from the original’s lines and the source’s wiki page, and it is separate from the draft. A To confirm row shows one line of it. Clicking the row selects it into the right pane: the summary in full, where it came from (Open original lines, Open wiki section), the quote, why, the fields, and what Add or Create draft will do. ↑/↓ move between rows and Return adds. The same on Slack, Jira, Confluence and Ask. Older items get their summary the first time you open them.
